headline: Protein language models underpin sequence-based prediction of stability and binding sites
label: Learned Protein Property Prediction
summary: Recent work tests whether sequence-only protein language models match structure-informed predictors for mutation stability effects and binding site detection.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned prediction of protein properties from sequence-derived representations, mostly protein language model embeddings, applied to mutation stability (ΔTm, ddG), binding sites (DeepPANB, IKANbind, DeepDPM for MoRFs), and functional annotation (SA-MTP, DeepAden, DeepKOALA). A notable contrast is that a sequence-only ESM2-650M model predicts mutation-induced ΔTm more accurately than structure-informed methods, whereas ThermoFusion combines ThermoMPNN structure embeddings with ESM2 sequence embeddings for ddG. What is new is the adaptation and augmentation layer: LoRA tuning with multi-representation fusion (LoMuS), biologically grounded augmentation in embedding space (fitness translocation), and optimal transport alignment of remote homologs over embeddings (OTalign). Interpretability methods such as DeepLIFT, SHAP and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks recur across the set. Not every item shares this thread; genomic language models (seqLens, EssTFNet) extend the approach to DNA.
